sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Both the worker and the soldier are larger than in the other species with the fungifaber type of enteric valve architecture (EVA); the alate, however, is almost impossible to distinguish from I. severus and I. ugandensis. The worker is large within the genus, and the distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth is the largest in the genus: WMlAmD = 0.23—0.25 mm. The soldier is large within the genus, its mandibles shorter than the head but the longest in relative terms within the genus: SMlL = 2.75—2.99 mm, SMlL/SHdL = 0.86—0.92 (about 85%—90% of the head length); the mandibles of some soldiers of I. bulbifrons may be equally long, but the enteric valve type differs. The gulamentum has almost straight, parallel sides, only slightly curved. The alate is medium-sized to large, and the distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth on both the left and the right mandible is the largest in the genus: IMlAmD = 0.26—0.28 mm; the ocelli are large and protruding, separated from the compound eye by less than 0.6 times the small ocellar diameter.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Coloration: head capsule well sclerotized and very dark, C6—C7; frontal gland pore concolorous or almost concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus C5—C6, slightly paler than the head capsule; antennae C5, slightly paler than the head capsule, without difference between the proximal and apical segments; pronotum C5—C6, concolorous with the postclypeus; meso- and metanotum C5—C6, concolorous with the pronotum; legs C4—C5, the tibiae concolorous with the femora; wings transparent with a brown to grey tinge (Cf3—Cf4), the costa darker; tergites C6, sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3—C4) and darker at the sides (C4—C6), the posterior sternites darker than the anterior ones (C4—C6). Setae: head capsule with a dense felt of short fine hairs, with conspicuous setae among them; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small setae, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip (visible above 50×); pronotum setae mainly on the margins, shorter in the middle; meso- and metanotum with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band (visible at 40—80×), the metanotum sometimes with large setae; legs hairy, the fore coxa with 4—10 stronger setae on the ridge and 1—4 ventrally; tibiae hairy, with 15—30 spines on the fore, mid and hind tibiae respectively, tibial spur formula 3/2/2, subapical spur formula 0/2/0. Structure: medium-sized to large within the genus; compound eyes large, short-oval; ocelli large, protruding, short to medium-oval, separated from the compound eye by less than 0.6 times the small ocellar diameter; frontal gland pore generally a small circular dot or an elongate mark; antennae 16-segmented (the queen in the type material lacks 3 segments through breakage); labrum domed, wider than long; left mandible apical tooth large within the genus, always more prominent than the first marginal tooth, with 3 marginal teeth (the second expressed as an undulating tooth margin, the third blunt-tipped), only the apical tooth sharp when unworn, the premolar partly hidden, the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process; right mandible apical tooth large within the genus, always more prominent than the first marginal tooth, with 2 marginal teeth, the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly; pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge; wings with R1 completely fused with the margin and sclerotized, Rs single and sclerotized, M and Cu unsclerotized or weakly sclerotized, with 3—4 and 10—13 branches respectively; gut not studied. Measurements (Table 18, mm): compound eye major diameter IEyD 0.49—0.53, head width including compound eyes IHdW 1.61—1.73, distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth IMlAmD 0.26—0.28, ocellus major diameter IOcD 0.21—0.23, postclypeus width IPcW 0.78—0.86, pronotum width IPnW 1.53—1.65, hind tibia length IT3L 1.45—2.08, left fore wing length to the suture IWgL 13.7—14.2 (n=3); indices IMlAmD/IMlmmD = 1.37—1.82.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Coloration: head capsule C4—C6, darkening with the time in preservation, with a smooth transition from a darker frons to a paler posterior; antennae and labrum about concolorous with the head capsule; mandibles dark (C7—C8), the base abruptly one shade paler (generally concolorous with the frons); thorax and legs paler than the head capsule (C3—C5), darkening with the time in preservation; abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Setae: head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of setae on the frons surrounds and hangs over the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small setae, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum with 7—10 large setae on each lateral lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with a few setae mainly on the margins; fore coxa with at least 1 fine seta and 2—3 spines on the ridge and 0—1 spines ventrally, the trochanter with several strong setae in a row or 5—6 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with tibial spur formula 3/2/2 and subapical spur formula 0/2/0 (the latter sometimes weak), each tibia with 9—14 spines; tergites with the large setae mainly on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae (erect or slightly inclined forward) and small setae directed posteriorly. Structure: large within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides mostly nearly parallel, slightly narrowing in the posterior 1/3 or 1/4, converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly convex or with a short straight stretch; the upper margin slightly concave, the angle between the protruding mandibles and the frons obtuse, the frons with a low gentle anterior swelling; gulamentum in ventral view with the sides nearly parallel, very slightly narrowing in the posterior half, the anterior half generally widening at sharp angles and even ear-like at the sides; antennae 15-segmented; labrum deeply forked, wider than long, the sides harp-shaped, the lobes angular, their tips fine, white or semitransparent, the anterior margin concave; mandibles sabre-like, the inner margin smooth, each with 1 distinct but very small marginal tooth (near the molar area), the mandibles shorter than the head but relatively the longest in the genus (85%—90% of the head length), the surface of both smooth and shining; right mandible equally or slightly more curved than the left; pronotum saddle-shaped, about 60% of the head width, the anterior margin straight or concave, the posterior margin straight; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut: enteric valve inserted on the left side of the abdomen, in the posterior half of the abdomen, best seen in ventral view; caecum small, three-lobed, near the middle of the abdomen; enteric valve primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion about 20% longer than the even ones, generally without a crest. Measurements (Table 18, mm): head dorsal concavity sagitta SHdC 0.01—0.04, head length SHdL 3.21—3.35, head width SHdW 2.20—2.39, left mandible ventral length SMlL 2.75—2.99, left mandible minor curvature SMlc 0.21—0.26, hind tibia length ST3L 1.70—1.92; indices SHdL/SHdW = 1.39—1.46, SMlc/SMlL = 0.08, SMlc/SMrc = 0.92—1.14.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Coloration: head capsule pale, darkening with the time in preservation; proximal antennal segments pale (C2—C3), the apical segment always one to two shades darker (C4—C5); thorax, tergites and legs pale, darkening with the time in preservation; abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Setae: head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small setae, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); tergites with scattered setae; fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3—4 spines on the ridge and 1 spine ventrally, the trochanter with 6—7 spines (all but 1 in a row); fore, mid and hind tibiae with tibial spur formula 3/2/2 and subapical spur formula 0/2/0, with 8—15 spines; tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae (erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented) and small setae directed posteriorly. Structure: large within the genus (but with much overlap with several species). Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles); antennae 14 or 14.5 segmented; labrum domed; left mandible apical tooth well developed and the largest in the genus, sharp when unworn, with 3 marginal teeth (the first well developed but blunt-tipped, the second expressed as an undulating tooth margin, the third blunt-tipped), the premolar partly hidden by the molar, the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process; right mandible apical tooth also the largest in the genus, the inner margin of the base sometimes undulating, with 2 marginal teeth, the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly; pronotum saddle-shaped, 70%—75% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut: enteric valve inserted on the left side of the abdomen, in the posterior half of the abdomen, best seen in ventral view; enteric valve primary cushions of the fungifaber type with trigonal symmetry, the downstream part of the odd cushion narrower, the crest as high as or higher than wide and bearing long strong setae, with 19—27 supporting setae on each side; secondary cushions (SC) broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed; caecum three-lobed, or one of the lobes slightly projecting forward, near the middle of the abdomen. Measurements (Table 18, mm): maximum head width WHdW 1.17—1.31, distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth WMlAmD 0.23—0.25, left mandible functional length WMlL 0.64—0.69, hind tibia length WT3L 1.38—1.48; mean length of enteric valve primary cushions 0.64—0.70, width 0.09—0.10, mean length of secondary cushions 0.50—0.62, width 0.27—0.42, odd primary cushion elongation index 6.39—8.27.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; measurements from Table 18 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
